solutions.explanation:
The final fold turns the left packet over onto the right packet. Its bottom square becomes the final top square, so track the bottom layers through the first three folds.

After step \(1\), the original bottom two rows remain against the table. Their bottom-layer numbers are \(9,10,11,12\) in the upper row and \(13,14,15,16\) in the lower row.

In step \(2\), the lower row folds over the upper row. The squares \(9,10,11,12\) therefore remain against the table, forming the bottom layers of the four packets from left to right.

In step \(3\), the right half folds over the left half. The two packets that stay against the table have bottom squares \(9\) and \(10\), from left to right.

Step \(4\) flips the left packet, whose bottom square is \(9\), onto the right packet. That bottom square becomes the very top. The answer is square \(\boxed{9}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
